text:
ConocoPhillips fell slightly today as oil prices declined on news that the G7 will release 100 million barrels of diesel reserves over the next four months—a direct supply increase aimed at easing fuel shortages tied to wars in Europe and the Middle East. This reserve release, announced as joint policy by major economies, puts downward pressure on crude prices, which in turn weighs on integrated oil companies' refining and upstream earnings.

The broader two-week decline of 3.85% reflects a tug-of-war between geopolitical risks that support oil prices (Middle East tensions, potential U.S. strikes on Iran, ongoing European conflict) and policy moves to increase supply that push prices down. The gap between U.S. crude ($96) and global Brent ($114) also signals market anxiety about regional supply disruptions, though today's G7 action favored the bearish side of that tension.
